_comment: South Carolina 2026, SC Housing. Scoring is Appendix C1 - 9% LIHTC (this file, the clean consolidated version despite its '-amendments' name; the redline companion reads 'Max - 65 70 points' where 70 is correct). Page numbers are PDF page indices; p.1 is a 27 January 2026 clarification sheet, so 'Page C1 - n' is PDF page n+1. TWO UNIVERSES: new construction (default track, Section III) and rehabilitation (track rehab, Section V, 'evaluated comparatively'). NO TOTAL IS STATED for either. Hand-summed before loading. New construction: 70 + 1 + 10 + 5 + 5 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 5 + 6 + 5 + 5 = 142. Rehabilitation: 10 + 9 + 3 + 1 = 23. The loader matched both. The table of contents (p.2) is stale against the body: its set-aside names and percentages (High-Demand New Construction 35-40%, Rehabilitation 20-25%, General New Construction) differ from the body's (Urban 35-40%, Rehabilitation 15-20%, Suburban 25-30%, Rural 5-10%, PHA one award), it has no Public Transportation item, and it calls III.G 'Project-Based Rent Assistance'. Recorded, not resolved. Thresholds are in SC_thresholds.json, cited to the QAP.

track_totals.note: New construction. No total stated. Computed 142, of which 70 is Distance to Amenities.
Rehabilitation applications are 'evaluated comparatively' on four criteria. No total stated. Computed 23. Alternative to new construction.

criteria.heading: Distance to Amenities
criteria.quote: A maximum of two (2) amenities per category can be used.

tiers.tier_label: Grocery, nearest band (Urban <1 mi, Suburban <2, Rural <3)

criteria.note: Points fall by driving-distance band (four bands per county group). Up to two amenities per category count, and one establishment may score in at most two categories: 2 x (10+7+7+6+4+4) = 76 against the stated 'Max - 70 points' in each of the three tables. The Suburban table's Public Facility row reads 4, 4, 2, 1 where the other tables read 4, 3, 2, 1. A 27 January 2026 clarification (p.1) excludes hair salons, barber shops, nail salons and post offices as retail.
